summary.text: The law of superposition says that in undeformed layers of rock or sediment, the oldest lie at the bottom and newer material stacks on top.
Danish scientist Nicolas Steno first proposed it in 1669, and William "Strata" Smith later used it to make the first geologic map of Britain.
It lets paleontologists rank the relative ages of fossils in layered rock, with the remains of the most archaic lifeforms in the lowest layers.

facts.label: Tilt limit
facts.value: Holds in sedimentary rock deformed no more than 90°

facts.label: Tricky cases
facts.value: Lava flows and ash falls may not obey it

items.prompt: In an undisturbed cliff of sedimentary rock, fossil shell A sits in a low layer and fossil shell B sits near the top. What can you conclude?

options.label: B's animal lived before A's
A's animal lived before B's
Both lived at the same time
Their order cannot be told

items.explain: In undeformed sedimentary rock the oldest layers are at the bottom, so fossils in lower layers are older than those above them.

items.prompt: On a dig, archaeologists find the silt that filled an old underground drain, lying beneath a layer of ground. When did that silt form compared with the ground above it?

options.label: Long before it, since it lies lower
At exactly the same moment
Some time after it
It cannot be compared at all

items.explain: Some archaeological layers are made by undercutting earlier ones; the silt back-fill of an underground drain forms after the ground immediately above it.

items.prompt: Builders cut a new window into an old standing wall. How does this fit the idea of superposition on a dig?

options.label: The window is a later change even though it is not on top
The window must be older because it sits low in the wall
The window and the wall count as the same layer in time
Windows break the rule, so the wall cannot be dated

items.explain: Adding doors and windows to standing structures is an example of non-vertical superposition: a later change that is not stacked on top.

items.prompt: Why does a geologist need extra care applying this law to a stack of lava flows and ash falls?

options.label: Volcanic rock never contains any layers at all
Lava always flows underneath older rock layers
Ash falls are too young to be studied as strata
Surface volcanic deposits layer in a different way

items.explain: Stratification behaves differently with surface-formed igneous deposits like lava flows and ash falls, so superposition may not always apply.

items.prompt: Over the years, burrowing animals and plant roots work their way through layered ground. What can that do to the record?

options.label: Turn the youngest layers into the oldest
Lock the layers firmly into their order
Disrupt the original natural layering
Add a fresh dated layer on the surface

items.explain: Original stratification from natural processes can later be disrupted or permutated by factors including animal interference and vegetation.

items.prompt: Fossils are sorted by layer through a thick stack of undeformed rock. What can this tell scientists about the species in it?

options.label: Exactly how many years each species lived
Which species lived together and which came one after another
Which species were the largest of their era
Which species are still alive today somewhere

items.explain: Superposition shows the fossil record through the layers, revealing which species coexisted and which existed successively.
